text:
jessica: build failed in prod CI, getting 403 when posting to /v1/deploys, started ~09:13 UTC

mike: can you paste the error payload or the curl that failed?

jessica: here's the error from the runner logs:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
date: Thu, 02 Mar 2024 09:13:10 GMT
content-type: application/json
{
  \"error\": \"insufficient_scope\",
  \"error_description\": \"token missing required scope: write:deploy\"
}
```

jessica: the token is coming from our CI token-broker (gha-proxy) that impersonates redwood-ci-bot

deploy-bot: :rotating_light: deploy attempt blocked (request_id=xyz-123) — policy=token-scope-check, required=[write:deploy], found=[read:logs,read:metrics]

mike: when did we change the broker scopes? tina do you know?

tina: we rolled a permissions pruning job last night to tighten ephemeral token scope defaults for non-deploy runners. intent was to reduce blast radius for PR preview jobs. I did not expect it to affect the prod deploy job.

infra-sre: quick check — can you run token introspect? from the runner: 
```
TOKEN=$CI_EPHEMERAL_TOKEN
curl -fsS -X POST https://tokens.internal.redwood/io/introspect -d \"token=$TOKEN\"
```

jessica: result pasted:
```
active: true
client_id: gha-proxy
sub: serviceAccount:redwood-ci-bot@infra
scopes: [read:logs, read:metrics]
aud: api.redwood-inference
exp: 1709457100
```

mike: I see aud is correct (api.redwood-inference) but scopes are missing write:deploy — so broker handed a too-restrictive token. Did the broker change the default scope set?

tina: yes, the broker now maps workflow->scope using the new policy table. looks like workflows with label `pr-preview` inherit a narrower default. but prod workflow should carry `deploy:true` label — investigating why it's not.

jessica: the GH job is using the gha-runner share and triggers a composite action `redwood/gha-proxy@v2` — might be picking up an older workflow name after the recent build-matrix refactor.

infra-sre: also seeing a separate anomaly — billing alert fired for the deploy project during the same window. might be unrelated but worth noting.

mike: high priority: we need prod deploys unblocked. options: (1) issue short-term override to treat tokens from gha-proxy as allowed for deploy endpoint (risky), (2) re-issue a token with explicit write:deploy via manual impersonation, (3) patch broker to include deploy scope for workflows in prod repo. Which is fastest?

tina: I can manually impersonate redwood-ci-bot and mint a token with write:deploy now: 
```
# infra box
gcloud iam service-accounts impersonate redwood-ci-bot@infra --scope=write:deploy --output=token
```

jessica: can you mint and paste into the failing runner? we have an in-flight release.

infra-sre: doing manual mint now and patching the runner env, applying token.

deploy-bot: automated note: deploy attempt retried with manual-token (request_id=xyz-124)

jessica: retry succeeded :tada: — thanks. we should still fix root cause so it doesn't happen again.

mike: agreed. tina — can you follow up with a broker policy change and a test job to assert prod workflows always get write:deploy? also add an integration test in infra that runs a dry-run deploy and checks token scopes.

tina: on it. immediate plan: revert the default scope pruning for `gha-proxy` unless `workflow` explicitly maps to narrower scopes. I'll open a PR to broker policy and a small GH action test.

infra-sre: action item for me to audit any other repos that use the gha-proxy action and might be impacted. I'll also check the billing alert correlation — looks like a spike due to a stuck runner loop earlier.

mike: note for long term: we still want least privilege, but prod deploys need an explicit allowlist or dedicated impersonation SA with pinned scopes to avoid accidental pruning. create a runbook for this scenario.

jessica: adding runbook entry now, linking to this thread. thanks all. :thumbsup:

tina: PR: https://git.internal.redwood/repo/infra/gha-proxy/pulls/371 — will include test and revert.

infra-sre: marking this resolved for now, will follow up in PR review. last check-in at 09:14:52 UTC
